observations: Snapshot custody verified: commit af9b1a5f is reachable from HEAD, parent matches 35ea20c3a, changes exactly 7 declared paths (no dispatch_queue.json), all six producer hashes match snapshot receipt.
J2-ATTACK-1 (honest path): emit_host_binding.sh runs successfully, producing values matching the host's identity surfaces (Adams-MacBook-Pro.local, /dev/disk5s1, /Volumes/SSD990).

J2-ATTACK-2 (forged receipt): a hand-written receipt with caller-supplied values passes binding_rule_v2 if the host_observation matches, but the source rule is violated (self-attestation gap, disclosed in package).

J2-ATTACK-3 (CWD-dependence): running the script from /tmp produces different filesystem values (/dev/disk3s5, /System/Volumes/Data) than from the worktree root (/dev/disk5s1, /Volumes/SSD990). The script captures the CWD's filesystem, not a fixed host identity.

J2-ATTACK-4 (PATH manipulation): prepending a fake hostname binary to PATH makes the script emit host_id='caller-controlled-hostname'. Prepending a fake df makes the script emit filesystem_id='/dev/fakedev' and filesystem_mount='/mnt/fake'. The script uses PATH-resolved binaries, not absolute paths. This contradicts the provenance claim 'never read from environment variables the caller controls' (PATH is such a variable). This is NOT disclosed in the package. Recorded as RT-J2-O1.

J2-ATTACK-5 (demo reality): demo values match the host's surfaces. Demo emitted_at (02:35:47Z) precedes producer receipt recorded_at (02:39:05Z) by ~3.5 min, consistent with the procedure. But a hand-written receipt with the same values is indistinguishable from a script-produced one.
J2-ATTACK-6 (cross-checks): independent cross-checks exist (hostname, df -P ., re-run script) but are after-the-fact, require same-host/same-CWD access, and are not automatic.
J3-CASE-A (caller-supplied binding): STOP fires correctly. binding_rule_v2 rejects inequality; caller_input_is_never_authoritative: true.
J3-CASE-B (missing binding): STOP fires correctly. missing_receipt_field: STOP. v2 parser accepts as schema-valid; STOP fires at binding-rule layer. Named weakening confirmed.
J3-CASE-C (v1 receipt under v2): STOP fires correctly against actual v1 corpus receipt (host_binding has only note key). Same named weakening.

J3-ESCAPE-HUNT: no new v2-specific escape found. Empty strings, null values, placeholders bypass missing-field STOP but are caught by binding_rule_v2 inequality (if evaluated). Duplicate keys: no discrepancy within one parser. Non-canonical encoding: normalization handles correctly.
RT-J3-O1: missing_receipt_field STOP fires on absence but not on emptiness or null. Gap in coverage; binding rule catches these values if evaluated. Non-blocking.
Proves-too-much: all three known-false objects rejected by my review method. Method is discriminating (catches env var control, fabricated demo values, presence-only STOPs). Control PASSES.

HOST-BINDING-ENFORCEABILITY: narrowed but LESS than package claims. PATH manipulation gap (RT-J2-O1) is not disclosed and is within the v5 threat model. Self-attestation gap (RT-J2-O2) is disclosed. CWD-dependence (RT-J2-O3) is partially disclosed.
